text: Two indistinguishable photons enter opposite ports of a 50/50 beam splitter (input |1,1>). What does the Hong-Ou-Mandel effect predict at the outputs?
choices: They always exit through separate ports, giving maximal coincidences
Each photon independently splits 50/50, giving |1,1> half the time
They bunch: |1,1> becomes (i/sqrt(2))(|2,0> + |0,2>) and the coincidence rate drops to zero
They annihilate each other and no photons emerge
explanation: Destructive interference of the both-transmit and both-reflect two-photon amplitudes forces the photons to leave together: |1,1> becomes (i/sqrt(2))(|2,0> + |0,2>), so coincidences vanish. Choice 0 is the opposite (distinguishable-particle) behavior; choice 1 ignores interference; photons are not destroyed (choice 3), they bunch.
